title: Harbinger is building the unsexy EVs that keep the economy moving
raw_text: While legacy automakers tap the brakes on electric vehicles, one startup is hitting the accelerator. Earlier this month, electric truck maker Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D round , capping a banner stretch that includes a $300 million order from FedEx and a new defense contract with the US military. Harbinger is stacking up wins by skipping the consumer EV hype cycle altogether and focusing on the unglamorous workhorses that keep the economy running: Class 4-6 delivery vans and box trucks. title: YouTube is reportedly preparing to settle social media addiction claims for $3 billion
raw_text: YouTube is preparing to pay $3 billion to thousands of school districts to settle claims that its "addictive design" harmed kids, according to Bloomberg . Sources tell the publication that YouTube reached the agreement "in principle," and that the deal would also include new safeguards for teens. The settlement would allow Google to avoid a wave of lawsuits filed by US school districts that accuse YouTube, Meta, Snap, and TikTok of negatively impacting the mental health of teen users. title: Multiplying your Switch 2’s storage costs less than usual right now
raw_text: Expanding your Nintendo Switch 2’s 256GB of built-in storage with a microSD card is pricier than it was with Nintendo’s original console. That’s because microSD Express cards , while physically identical to ones you might have lying around, have faster read and write speeds. Thankfully, Samsung’s 256GB model has dropped to $44.99 at Amazon ahead of Black Friday, which is a few bucks off its usual price but still well below its $79.99 MSRP. Sandisk’s 256GB card, meanwhile, is available for $49.99 ($10 off Amazon’s typical list price) from Amazon and Sandisk , if you prefer one brand over the other for some reason. For those who don’t want to think about upgrading their Switch 2’s storage again, both brands’ 512GB microSD Express cards are selling for a fair $99.99 on Amazon . That gives you double the storage for roughly twice the price of a 256GB card, as it should be. title: Google says it’s going to shut off Google Assistant on smart speakers next year
raw_text: Google is announcing some significant changes to its smart home software. Starting next year, the company will shut down the Nest app in favor of the Google Home app and retire Google Assistant on its smart home devices. The Nest app shutdown takes place on January 25th, 2027, meaning you'll have to manage your Nest products, including Nest thermostats, cameras, and Nest Protect alarms, from the Google Home app instead. If you get the Google Home app set up, Google will move over your Nest devices, including cameras and video history, to the Home app on that January 25th date. title: Voor Red Bull is compute ook een tco-race
raw_text: Interview | Martin Galpin, hoofd divisie Software Engineering De Formule 1 staat bekend als een technologische speeltuin waar teams voortdurend investeren in software, simulaties en data-analyse. Toch vormt niet de technologie niet de grootste uitdaging maar kostenbeheersing. Volgens Martin Galpin, hoofd van de divisie Software Engineering bij Oracle Red Bull Racing en Red Bull Technology, draait het steeds vaker om de vraag hoe je binnen het budgetplafond de juiste keuzes maakt. Martin Galpin Het F1-seizoen zit er bijna op met de jonge Kimi Antonelli uit de Mercedes-stal als nieuwe wereldkampioen. Voor Oracle Red Bull Racing ligt er nog de sportieve uitdaging om de laatste Grand Prix’s te winnen, te beginnen met de Grand Prix van Las Vegas op het Las Vegas Strip Circuit dit weekeinde, zeker nu Max Verstappen weer in de ’the winning mood’ is. Technologie is daarbij niet meer weg te denken en kan in deze sport, waarin milliseconden tellen, de doorslag voor de overwinning geven. Een belangrijk rol daarbij is weggelegd voor de divisie Software Engineering bij Red Bull Racing en Red Bull Technology. Hoofd is Martin Galpin, van jongs af aan groot autorace-liefhebber die na zijn informaticastudie op de universiteit vrijwel direct bij Red Bull is gaan werken. Zijn softwareteam, met het Britse Milton Keynes als standplaats, heeft een focus op aerodynamica, voertuigdynamica, simulatoren, racestrategie, machine learning, data science en softwareontwikkeling.
